name: Brazil
note: A physician completes the federal Declaração de Óbito, and a relative or other listed declarant registers the death at the Registro Civil de Pessoas Naturais, in principle within 24 hours. The registry's certidão is required for burial. Each registered death must then go to the INSS through the federal SIRC within one business day, to the electoral justice monthly and to IBGE quarterly. Everything here is unverified: all official Brazilian law hosts were unreachable from this session.

steps.title: Physician completes the Declaração de Óbito
steps.who: The attending physician; for violent deaths the Instituto Médico-Legal; where there is no physician, two qualified persons who saw the death.
steps.summary: The federal standard Declaração de Óbito is mandatory nationwide for collecting death data and is required to draw up the death registration.

steps.title: Violent deaths go to forensic autopsy
steps.who: Police authority and the official forensic medical service (IML).
steps.summary: Deaths from violent causes are examined by official forensic experts under the criminal procedure code before the death is registered.

steps.title: Declare the death at the Registro Civil de Pessoas Naturais
steps.who: The persons listed in art. 79 in order (head of household, spouse, children, relatives, hospital administrators, attending physician, neighbours, police for found bodies).
steps.trigger: The death, with the Declaração de Óbito.

deadline.text: 24 hours, extendable to 15 days (longer for places far from the registry)

steps.summary: The death is registered at the civil registry of the place of death (or residence) in principle within 24 hours; where that is impossible, within the art. 50 periods (15 days, longer for distant places).

steps.title: Hospital administrators as declarants
steps.who: Administrators of hospitals and similar establishments.
steps.summary: Hospital administrators are among the persons bound to declare the death.

steps.title: No burial without the registry's death certidão
steps.who: The registry officer (oficial de registro civil).
steps.summary: No burial without a certidão from the civil registry issued after the death entry is drawn up.

steps.title: Certidão de óbito for any applicant
steps.who: Any person, without stating a reason.
steps.summary: Registry certificates may be requested by anyone without stating the reason or interest.

steps.title: Registry sends the death to the INSS through SIRC within one business day
steps.who: The titular of the Registro Civil de Pessoas Naturais.

deadline.text: within one business day of registration

steps.summary: The registry must transmit registered deaths to the INSS through SIRC within one business day; non-compliance is penalised.

steps.title: SIRC distributes registry data to federal bodies
steps.who: SIRC (managed by the federal government with a steering committee), receiving data from all civil registries.
steps.summary: SIRC collects civil-registration data from the registries and makes it available to federal bodies.

steps.title: Registry reports deaths to the Justiça Eleitoral
steps.who: Civil registry officers, to the electoral judge.
steps.trigger: Deaths of citizens of voting age registered in the month.

deadline.text: by the 15th of the following month

steps.summary: Officers must report each month the deaths of persons eligible to vote, for cancellation of their registration.

steps.title: Quarterly returns to IBGE
steps.summary: Registries send IBGE quarterly returns of births, marriages and deaths for vital statistics.

steps.title: Receita Federal marks the CPF "titular falecido"
steps.who: Receita Federal do Brasil, from SIRC/registry data or a request by the family or estate.
steps.summary: The CPF of a deceased person is shown as "titular falecido"; the normative instruction and data route were not read.

steps.title: CRC Nacional: electronic registry network and certificates
steps.who: Civil registries through the Central de Informações de Registro Civil (CRC), under CNJ rules, within the electronic registry system (SERP).
steps.summary: Registries are interconnected through the CRC, which lets certificates be requested electronically from any registry; the CNJ provisions were not read.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: In principle within 24 hours; where impossible, within the art. 50 periods (15 days, longer for distant places).

informantDuty.note: An ordered list in art. 79 runs from the head of household and relatives to hospital administrators, physicians, neighbours and police.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of the Declaração de Óbito; violent deaths go to the forensic service (IML).

electronicRegistration.note: Registries operate in the national electronic system (SERP/CRC) and transmit to SIRC, but the declaration is made at the registry.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No single population register in the legal sense; SIRC aggregates civil-registration data and the CPF base is kept by the Receita Federal.

governmentPropagation.note: Registries must send deaths to the INSS through SIRC within one business day and report monthly to the electoral justice.

certificateAccess.note: Anyone may request a certidão without stating a reason.

privateSectorVerification.note: Not established; the CPF status "titular falecido" is visible in the Receita's public status query, but no source was read.
